title: Operations Management Adventure 2: Lean & Quality
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Kaizen, JIT, TQM and Six Sigma — the lean and quality toolkit.
meta_desc: IBDP Business Management Ops: lean (Kaizen, JIT) and quality management (TQM, Six Sigma).
final_note: You learned lean production tools and the two main quality management systems.

concepts.def: Workers meet to solve quality issues

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lean came from the Toyota Production System.

Lean attacks the seven muda (wastes): transport, inventory, motion, waiting, overproduction, over-processing, defects.

Tools include Kaizen, JIT, 5S, kanban and andon cords.

Kaizen means 'change for the better' — many small workforce-led improvements rather than top-down upheaval.

Just-in-time aligns stock arrival to production. Less stock means lower storage cost but high vulnerability — one supplier delay halts the line.

TQM (Deming) embeds quality across every department: 'right first time'.

Six Sigma (Motorola, 1986) uses statistics to reach 3.4 defects per million opportunities through DMAIC: Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control.
